key_insight: A SCAPS-1D optimization study shows that a Cu2NiGeS4 absorber paired with In2S3 and MoTe2 charge-selective layers can theoretically deliver much higher thin-film solar-cell efficiency than previously reported designs.
engineering_relevance: The work provides a device-level roadmap for improving quaternary chalcogenide photovoltaics through absorber, interface, and transport-layer engineering.
method: Simulated an In2S3/Cu2NiGeS4/MoTe2 heterostructure in SCAPS-1D
Optimized thickness, doping, defect density, recombination, resistance, temperature, and illumination
Analyzed band alignment, electric fields, carrier profiles, and generation-recombination behavior
evidence_signal: The optimized device is reported to reach 28.44% PCE with VOC = 0.984 V, JSC = 34.39 mA/cm2, and FF = 84.04% under AM1.5G at 300 K.
watch_item: The results are purely computational, so experimental validation is still needed to confirm material quality, interface stability, and achievable defects/resistances in real devices.
paper_title: Device Engineering and Performance Optimization of Cu2NiGeS4 Thin-Film Solar Cells with In2S3/MoTe2 Charge-Selective Layers: A Computational Study
